findings.location: scripts/agent_loop.py _overridden; README 'A gate's FAIL is never overridden'
findings.finding: GATE_OVERRIDDEN does not follow the failed bytes through read-only tool outputs, although UNGATED_CONSUMPTION's reach now does (R1-3). A read-only tool that reads the artefact before the FAIL carries it past the FAIL: patch passes schema-check, read-file reads it, unit-tests FAILs patch, then write-file consumes the read's output: accepted (N01). A model step consuming that output after the FAIL is accepted and delivered (N02). The same trace with the read placed after the FAIL is refused (N02b), so the result depends only on timing. N01 is the write form of the refused vector 'delivering an artefact one gate passed and another failed', and it contradicts MAS-RA-001 rule 7 (a deterministic FAIL decides wherever it was observed), H13 ('a probabilistic detector cannot override a deterministic denial') and HERMES p. 15.
findings.requiredChange: After a FAIL, treat every step in the failed bytes' read-only reach as failed. That reach is the steps holding those bytes, plus the outputs of read-only tools that read any of them, whenever produced. No later write, model step or delegation may consume such a step, except a revision of the subject, and none may be delivered. State in the README whether a revision may consume these derived outputs. Add N01 and N02 as GATE_OVERRIDDEN vectors.

findings.location: scripts/agent_loop.py _View.unknown_unsafe, _unsafe_retry, _must_hand_off; README 'Bounded retry, then a human' and 'Delegation'
findings.finding: A parent may retry a DELEGATE whose child ended ABORTED. Of the in-loop side-effect retry rules, only the one for an UNKNOWN write without idempotency reaches into the child. So retrying the delegation re-runs a child's unresolved write that the same retry inside one loop could not. (1) A child's receipt-keyed write-file ends UNKNOWN and a DYNAMIC hook aborts the child; the parent re-delegates and the new child writes under another input, that is another receipt key: accepted (N25). In one loop the vector 'a receipt-keyed write retried with another input' is refused. (2) A child's non-idempotent post-ticket ends ERROR with no evidence of no effect and the child is aborted; the new child posts again: accepted (N26), while the in-loop case is refused. The same path also retries around a DYNAMIC hook's abort of a child, although the README says 'abort wins' (N07 accepted). And it gives a retried FAILED child a fresh revision budget on the same task (N24: two rounds under revision.rounds 1). R1-5 closed the HANDED_OFF path only. H11: 'Non-idempotent actions retry only with an authoritative receipt lookup proving no prior effect'.
findings.requiredChange: Retry a DELEGATE only when every in-loop side-effect retry rule would allow it. The simplest form: never retry a DELEGATE whose child ended after a step that must hand off (HANDED_OFF, or a hook abort following such a step), and make the parent hand off. Closing R2-3 also closes this part. State whether a child's HOOK_ABORT under a DYNAMIC hook may be retried around, and how revision rounds compose with the parent's retries. Add N25 and N26 as refusal vectors.

findings.location: scripts/agent_loop.py _handoff; README 'Every failing step is retried or hands off'
findings.finding: After a step that must hand off, a hook abort ends the loop in place of the human hand-off. An UNKNOWN non-idempotent post-ticket followed by the budget-stop abort ends ABORTED/HOOK_ABORT and is accepted (N09). The kernel's own abort at the same point is refused (vector 'retries spent and the loop aborts instead of handing off'). The sources disagree with this. Q-MAS8-C: 'then hand-off to a human'. H10: a non-idempotent ambiguous outcome 'pauses as INPUT_REQUIRED/operator review'. H11: OUTCOME_UNKNOWN 'requires operator/owner reconciliation'. The ABORTED alternative came from round 1's own suggestion for R1-7. The UNKNOWN case and the delegation path (R2-2) show it needs a limit.
findings.requiredChange: At least after an UNKNOWN side effect, require HANDED_OFF; an aborting hook can be recorded before the final HANDOFF step. Otherwise, state three things in the README: a hook abort ends the loop without a human; OUTCOME_UNKNOWN reconciliation stays with H10 and H11, outside the trace; and this narrows Q-MAS8-C's 'then hand-off to a human', which is an owner point. Add N09 with its decided result.

findings.location: scripts/agent_loop.py _consumers; loop-trace.schema.json step consumes/produces; README 'Deterministic gates interleave'
findings.finding: GATE, HOOK and HANDOFF steps may carry `consumes` and `produces`, but neither has a defined meaning on them, and the consumer reach follows only TOOL steps. So a HOOK or GATE step can relay an ungated model artefact to a write. A HOOK step that consumes the ungated patch and produces its digest, then is consumed by write-file: accepted (N04). A GATE step on another subject that declares consumes [patch], then is consumed by write-file: accepted (N04b). The reach is also keyed by step ID, while GATE_OVERRIDDEN is now keyed by bytes: a trusted read-only tool step whose output digest equals an ungated model artefact's feeds a write (N29 accepted).
findings.requiredChange: Refuse `produces` and `consumes` on GATE, HOOK and HANDOFF steps (a gate's subject and a hook's event live in `detail`), or follow the reach through every step kind. State in the README that the rule covers declared consumption only, or key it by bytes as GATE_OVERRIDDEN now is. Add N04 as a refusal vector.

findings.finding: A delegation can reach writes: the child runs under the same profile with its write tools, and its steps cannot name the parent's. Yet a DELEGATE counts as a consumer only of a model artefact, and only when it consumes it directly. An ungated model artefact read by a read-only tool whose output a DELEGATE consumes is accepted (N05). An untrusted web-search output handed straight to a DELEGATE is accepted (N06). Inside the child, nothing that came from the parent is visible to the child's own gate rule. So the R1-3 and R1-9 fixes can be bypassed through delegation.
findings.requiredChange: Treat a DELEGATE like a WRITE tool in the reach: a consumer of both producer kinds, directly or through read-only tool outputs. Add N05 and N06 as UNGATED_CONSUMPTION vectors, or state the gap in 'Not claimed'.

findings.finding: The revision budget binds declared revisions only. A fresh model step that consumes the failing GATE step, and so its diagnosis, without `revises` is a revision in all but name. Under revision.rounds 1: the draft fails, its one revision fails, then such a step passes and is delivered (N03 accepted: two rounds). The same works with no declared revision at all (N03b accepted). Unlike the disguised model retries that 'Not claimed' covers, this is detectable, because the gate step is named in `consumes`. It repeats R1-2's bypass.
findings.requiredChange: Allow only a revision of the gate's subject, or a retry of that revision, to consume a failed GATE step. Alternatively, count any model step that consumes a failed gate as a round of its subject's chain, or extend 'Not claimed' to undeclared revisions. Add N03.

findings.finding: The outcome of a HOOK or HANDOFF step has no consequence. The egress-guard HOOK step ERRORs, and the post-ticket call it guards goes ahead to COMPLETED (N11 accepted). That fails open, while H13 keeps INPUT and RUNTIME guardrails fail-closed ('a detector error stays degraded and non-releasing'). A HANDOFF step that ERRORed still yields HANDED_OFF (N12 accepted), so the status can claim a hand-off that did not happen.
findings.requiredChange: Define these outcomes. A HOOK step that is not OK makes the loop abort or hand off (fail closed), and HANDED_OFF needs an OK HANDOFF step. Alternatively, restrict HOOK and HANDOFF steps to OK in the shape and say how a failing hook is recorded. Add vectors.

findings.finding: The README says an OK step's output is its artefact and that ERROR means the operation did not complete. Yet a MODEL step that ended ERROR may carry `produces`, be gated, and be consumed by a write (N14 accepted). R1-8 fixed delivery only.
findings.requiredChange: Refuse `produces` on a MODEL step that is not OK, or state what a non-OK step's artefact is and who may consume it.

findings.location: scripts/agent_loop.py _tool_input, _unsafe_retry; README 'Model output is data' and 'Side effects'
findings.finding: The only way to record that a call was not launched is `inputValid` false. H11 lists policy, approval, artifact, RBAC, network-intent and isolation failures as preventing launch too (its DENIED state). A policy-denied receipt-keyed write with a schema-valid input therefore counts as launched, and its retry with a corrected input is refused UNKNOWN_SIDE_EFFECT_RETRIED (N30). A denied NONE write likewise needs a receiptRef before it may be retried.
findings.requiredChange: Record a pre-launch refusal separately from schema validity, for example with a `launched` flag, or by treating FAIL with no output and no receipt as not launched. Or state the limitation.

findings.location: scripts/agent_loop.py _terminal; README 'Hook placement' (Not claimed) and 'Terminal status'
findings.finding: A HANDOFF-event hook can be recorded only before the HANDOFF step it observes. Recorded after it, the trace is refused TERMINAL_STATUS (N13); recorded before, it passes (N13b). For other events, after-event hooks follow their operation's step (TR_OK's TOOL_RESULT_AFTER hook follows the tool step). Yet the README says hook placement is not checked.
findings.requiredChange: Say in the README that the HANDOFF step is always the last step and that a HANDOFF hook is recorded before it. Or let observing hooks follow the HANDOFF step.

findings.location: README 'The loop trace' (MODEL detail) and 'The loop profile' (Tools)
findings.finding: Three wording points. (1) 'Secrets never reach a model' overstates the check, which only requires a model step's declared credentialRefs to be empty; a secret in a tool output that a model reads is left to H11's redaction. (2) H11's four-valued sideEffect (none, reversible, compensatable, irreversible) is collapsed to READ_ONLY/WRITE without a stated mapping. (3) H11's per-execution human approval for irreversible tools is not recorded in a call. The README leaves approvals to H11, but 'Not claimed' does not say so.
findings.requiredChange: Narrow the secrets sentence to what is checked. Add one sentence mapping H11's side-effect classes onto READ_ONLY/WRITE. Add approvals to 'Not claimed'.

dispositions.evidence: _overridden keys the rule by the subject's bytes. P01 (fresh copy) and P02 (same-bytes revision) are now refused GATE_OVERRIDDEN, and the vectors 'a fresh model step reproducing failed bytes' and 'a revision returning the failed bytes' pin them. Bytes derived through a read-only tool before the FAIL still escape; that is the new finding R2-1.

_revision_bound allows one non-retry revision per step and bounds the chain. P03 and P04 are refused REVISION_BOUND; two sibling vectors pin them (rounds 1 and 3). P31 (a retry of a revision) is still accepted. Undeclared revisions that consume the failing gate remain open: R2-6.

_consumers follows read-only tool outputs to writes, and DELEGATE is a direct consumer of model artefacts. P05 and P06 are refused UNGATED_CONSUMPTION; TR_READ_UNGATED stays valid, and the README states that model consumers are direct only. Indirect delegation and relay through HOOK or GATE steps remain open: R2-4, R2-5.

The new code DELEGATION requires the parent's profile digest, a child start no earlier than its DELEGATE step, and disjoint grants. P10 and P15 are refused DELEGATION. P11 (a child recording the parent's DYNAMIC hook) is accepted. P12 is refused (the child's own conflicting profile fails UNKNOWN_REFERENCE; another profile fails DELEGATION). P13 is refused BUDGET_EXCEEDED, so the child's iterations are carried. A LOCAL hook in a child is refused HOOK_NOT_REGISTERED, and N18 (a child holding a later parent grant) is refused DELEGATION.

P08 (re-delegation after the child HANDED_OFF) is refused HANDOFF_MISSING, and P09 (re-delegation after the child's UNKNOWN non-idempotent write) is refused UNKNOWN_SIDE_EFFECT_RETRIED, both pinned by vectors. The same class continues through children that ended ABORTED: R2-2 (N25, N26).

The README defines the outcomes. PROVENANCE requires a receipt on every OK write (P16 refused). A NONE write is retried only after a gateway refusal or with receipt evidence (P17 refused, N15 accepted), and a receipt-keyed retry needs the same input (vector). Pre-launch policy denial is a NOTE (R2-9); the delegation path is R2-2.

Every unretried failing step other than a gate, hook or hand-off must hand off, and FAILED needs a gate that did not pass. P20 and P21 are refused HANDOFF_MISSING. The disguised-retry rule was removed, and P27 and P28 are still refused HANDOFF_MISSING. The ABORTED-by-hook alternative (as round 1 suggested) needs a limit for UNKNOWN side effects: R2-3.
COMPLETED needs the delivered MODEL step to be OK. P22 is refused TERMINAL_STATUS and pinned by a vector. A non-OK step's artefact can still be consumed: NOTE R2-8.
Untrusted tool outputs are producers. P07 is refused UNGATED_CONSUMPTION and TR_UNTRUSTED_GATED is valid. The delegation bypass is R2-5.

check_profile refuses a SUPPLY_OUTPUT hook beside another hook's MODIFY_INPUT on one event: P33 is refused HOOK_CONFLICT, and one hook doing both is valid (vector). The README now says the 13 events adapt JAZ's and names the four operations; checked against JAZ p. 14 (Enter/Send/Complete/Exit per operation and LLMQueryRetry).

An ABORT on HANDOFF is SHAPE in both the schema and the model (P23). Two ABORT hooks on one event are recorded as the trailing steps (P26 accepted, TR_TWO_ABORTS valid), and aborts on two events are refused TERMINAL_STATUS (vector).

V058 uses SUPPLY_OUTPUT, and the attempt-skip vector runs under the 3-retry profile. The builder asserts isolation for every rule-phase refusal. My own re-run (P38) found 0 deviations: every case passes with its rule disabled or falls to its declared alsoRefusedBy (V073, V132, V138, V139).
The README cites Harness-Zero p. 8 for the turn limit; verified ('exhaust the turn limit', p. 8).

P14 is refused DUPLICATE_ID, P15 DELEGATION and P18 BUDGET_EXCEEDED. Grants are checked across the parent and its children (vector and N18). 'Not claimed' now covers cross-loop timing and grants across unrelated loops.

A gateway-refused call (inputValid false, FAIL, no output, no receipt) is recordable: P19 accepted, TR_REFUSED_CALL valid, and N16 (a refused call with an output) refused INVALID_TOOL_INPUT. The README states the SUPPLY_OUTPUT accounting under MODEL.
loop-profile.schema.json has `default` 1 on retry.stepRetries and 3 on revision.rounds, and the README says a producer writes both fields.
